note: Areas of herdrup's ipad-pro-13 references (1376x1032 pt) that are not compared, in reference points with the status bar included. Measured on the 12 PNGs at herdrup 7d802ebb, byte-identical to the pinned 75e117e2 (main, #564). Add a rect here to stop comparing an area.

rects.name: status-bar
rects.why: iPadOS status bar (manifest statusBar.heightPoints 32). refdiff -crop-top-pt 32 already cuts it; listed so the mask names everything not compared.

rects.name: tab-bar-glass
rects.why: The sidebar tab bar's Liquid Glass capsule with its Agents/Gram/Settings items. herdrup 9845ecf App/HerdrApp.swift 2818-2843 (sidebarTabBar): 62 pt tall (DesignTokens.Size.tabBar), 14 pt from the column's sides, at most 320 pt wide (tabBarMaxWidth); the sidebar is 320 pt (sidebarMin, HerdrApp.swift 2487), so the capsule spans x 14-306. In the 11 non-rail 9845ecf references every pixel differing from the sidebar fill #13162A in that band spans x 13.5-306.5, y 938-1000 pt: the source span plus its half-point anti-aliased edge. The fill around it is exact (no shadow).

rects.name: loading-detail-field
rects.why: The detail column's glyph field (x 320 pt to the right edge, from the status bar to 20 pt above the bottom). The detail column starts at the 320 pt sidebar's edge (herdrup 9845ecf HerdrApp.swift 2487, sidebarMin); in ref-ipad-pro-13-loading.png the sidebar fill #13162A ends at px 639 and ground starts at px 640 on every row. In the loading reference it is plain ground only because the capture froze the window's layers before the field's first resting picture arrived (reference README, `loading`). herdrup draws the field while loading, and so does the desktop. Compared in every other state.

rects.name: window-resize-corner
rects.why: iPadOS's bottom-right window-resize arc, system chrome drawn over the app (bright pixels x 1348-1371.5, y 1004-1027.5 pt in all six states), plus its anti-aliasing.
